correctness.rationale: The proof independently constructs the weighted empirical distribution \(F_N\), whose mean is \(1-e^{-x}\) and whose squared standard-deviation coefficient is \(a_N^2=H_N^{(2s)}/(H_N^{(s)})^2\). In time windows of width \(O(a_N)\), the centered-increment variance is \(O(a_N^3)\); a monotone grid argument yields the quantile linearization with derivative \(1-\theta\). Bounded-vector Lindeberg gives the joint Gaussian law precisely when the squared coefficient sums diverge, while \(\ell^2\) coefficient convergence gives the joint Bernoulli series when they converge. Power-sum asymptotics establish each constant. A nonzero third cumulant except at the half-threshold, where the fourth cumulant is nonzero, proves non-Gaussianity. The packaged checker successfully reproduced 159 checks (140 exact nested-level moment assertions, 12 exact cumulants, 7 deterministic normalization trends); finite checks are supportive only. The domain is fixed \(0\le s<1\), \(\lambda>0\) and finitely many fixed interior thresholds.

originality.rationale: The main 2026 paper proves only a homogeneous-rate law of large numbers in Theorem 4.1; its Zipf theorems use aligned heterogeneous arrival probabilities, unlike homogeneous rates here. General weighted empirical expansion work assumes bounded rescaled observation weights, whereas the positive-s Zipf weights have diverging rescaled maximum and exhibit a non-Gaussian limiting series. Ordinary empirical-process Gaussian approximation results and weighted quantile estimators do not state this complete three-phase quorum-time theorem. Targeted record and literature searches found no direct covering result. Generic unindexed triangular-array quantile theory remains a genuine priority risk.

value.rationale: The motivating homogeneous-clock theorem establishes a universal deterministic limit for all diffuse weight vectors without resolving which weight heterogeneities alter fluctuations. Zipf weights remain individually vanishing throughout \(s<1\), yet the second-order laws undergo a sharp boundary at \(s=1/2\): Gaussian fluctuations below, a logarithmic Gaussian scale at equality, and a non-Gaussian Bernoulli series above. The result gives a complete finite-dimensional law for any fixed finite collection of quorum thresholds and sharp Gaussian covariance constants. This is a structural, naturally motivated limit-law classification, not an arbitrary parameter slice or a variance-only observation.
